readings_chosen: Sentence 1: 'described ... in her notebook' can be read as the describing being located in the notebook, or as the notebook being where the writing went. Chosen: a happening 'technician DESCRIBED routine' with the location sent to the bin, since where things are is outside the language; the notebook still gets a thing line because it is in the happening.

Sentence 2: 'in the order she had tested them' can make the testing part of the routine or prior background. Chosen: prior background, because 'had tested' is past perfect, so h3 and its result r1 are GIVEN; the order is kept as the order of the chain, and link l1 records that the listing needed that result.

Sentence 3: 'the temperature of the incubator' can be read as a thing (a reading taken) or as a quality of the incubator. Chosen: a thing, described as the incubator's temperature; the times of day went to the bin.

Sentences 1 and 4: the response class of a person can be not stated, or the language's own class for a person. Chosen: heavy and standing, marked usual case after the language's fixed list, since the text is silent on how a person answers a press.

Sentence 4: 'The notebook also described' can be read as the technician describing or as the notebook as doer. Chosen: the notebook as DOER of h5, matching the text's own wording; 'the supplier had sent' is GIVEN background (past perfect); 'each printed in blue ink' is a GIVEN fact about the labels.

Sentences 2-5: the details can be read as the contents of the routine's description (a told notebook world) or as the narrator's own statements. Chosen: the narrator's own statements in the actual ledger, since the main verbs are the technician's writing acts asserted directly; the background facts (testing, sending, cleaning) are GIVEN, not TOLD.

Sentence 5: 'she noted that the fume cupboard had been cleaned' can be read as the cleaning being asserted by the narrator or as only what the note said. Chosen: the noting as a CLAIMED happening whose content is the cleaning, and the cleaning as a GIVEN fact with no named cleaner, following the unnamed-actor precedent; 'at the end of the page' went to the bin.
